pattern: Contended single value with many watchers: make every write a conditional update in one source of truth, record it append-only in the same transaction, then fan the committed change out asynchronously through pub/sub to long-lived connections; time-driven state changes are guarded by the write path itself, not by a timer.

tips.nudge: What is the one action that changes an auction?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for placing a bid and when it is accepted.
tips.show: F2: Place a bid; it is accepted only if it beats the current highest bid by the minimum increment and the auction is open.

tips.nudge: Someone has the auction page open in the last minute. What should they see?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for seeing new highest bids as they happen.
tips.show: F3: Watchers see the current highest bid update live (within ~1 s) without refreshing.

tips.nudge: What happens when the clock runs out?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for ending the auction and deciding the winner.
tips.show: F4: The auction closes at its end time; later bids are rejected; the highest bidder wins and both parties are notified.

tips.nudge: Two bidders submit at the same millisecond. What must never happen?
tips.hint: State the consistency guarantee for the highest bid as a non-functional requirement.
tips.show: N1: Strong consistency per auction: concurrent bids are ordered, exactly one is the highest, and an accepted bid is never overwritten by a lower one.

tips.nudge: A seller claims a bid was ignored. What do you need to show them?
tips.hint: Add a non-functional requirement about keeping every bid.
tips.show: N2: Durable: an acknowledged bid is never lost, and every bid is kept in an immutable audit log for disputes.

tips.nudge: Start from bids per day.
tips.hint: bid_qps = bids per day / 86,400 s, then a peak factor.
tips.show: bid_qps = 10M / day ≈ 120 /s; peak ×10 ≈ 1,200 /s; a hot auction alone can see ~100 /s at the end.

tips.nudge: One bid on a popular auction has to reach how many screens?
tips.hint: Messages per second = bids per second on hot auctions × watchers per auction.
tips.show: fanout_msgs = 50 bids/s × 10k watchers ≈ 500k messages/s for one hot auction.

checks.label: Bid history storage over a year estimated

tips.nudge: Every bid is kept. How much is that per year?
tips.hint: Bids per day × 365 × bytes per bid.
tips.show: bid_storage_year = 10M × 365 × 200 B ≈ 730 GB/year.

tips.nudge: What does the client send when someone clicks 'Bid'?
tips.hint: A POST on the auction with an amount, safe to retry, answering accepted or outbid.
tips.show: POST /auctions/{id}/bids {amount} + Idempotency-Key → 201 {bid_id, high_bid} | 409 {current_high_bid}

tips.nudge: How does the browser receive updates it didn't ask for?
tips.hint: A long-lived GET (SSE) or a WebSocket upgrade per auction.
tips.show: GET /auctions/{id}/stream (SSE, or a WebSocket) → events {high_bid, bidder_alias, bid_count, ends_at}

tips.nudge: What do you store for the auction, and what for each bid?
tips.hint: An auction row with the current high bid and a version, plus an append-only bids table.
tips.show: auctions(id, seller_id, status, ends_at, high_bid, high_bidder, version); bids(id, auction_id, bidder_id, amount, status, created_at), append-only.

checks.label: Concurrent writes designed as their own part

tips.nudge: Two bids of $105 and $110 arrive together on a $100 auction. Treat that as its own sub-problem.
tips.hint: Compare a row lock, an optimistic compare-and-set on the high bid, and serializing bids per auction through a partitioned log.
tips.show: Part 'Bid placement': a conditional UPDATE auctions SET high_bid=… WHERE id=… AND status='open' AND now() < ends_at AND :amount >= high_bid + increment; insert the bid and an outbox row in the same transaction.

checks.label: Live updates designed as their own part

tips.nudge: A hot auction has 10k watchers. Give delivering its updates its own part.
tips.hint: Compare polling, long polling, and push over SSE/WebSockets with a pub/sub channel per auction.
tips.show: Part 'Real-time fan-out': push servers hold SSE connections and subscribe to Redis Pub/Sub channel auction:{id}; a publisher forwards BidPlaced events from Kafka to the channel.

checks.label: Ending auctions designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Ten million auctions each end at their own second. What ends them?
tips.hint: Compare a periodic scan, per-auction timers/delayed messages, and a time-indexed poller; decide what actually rejects late bids.
tips.show: Part 'Auction close': late bids are rejected by the bid's own now() < ends_at predicate; a scheduler polls an ends_at index every second and a closer worker finalises the winner and emits AuctionClosed.

tips.nudge: Millions of open connections and thousands of API calls: what spreads them?
tips.hint: Stateless services and push servers behind something that distributes requests.
tips.show: Load balancer / API gateway in front of the auction, bid and push services (sticky for SSE/WebSocket connections).

checks.label: Read path can absorb page views

tips.nudge: Item pages are viewed far more than they are bid on.
tips.hint: Put something in front of the database for auction pages.
tips.show: Redis (and a CDN for images) for auction pages; live price comes from the push channel.

tips.nudge: No user request arrives at the moment an auction ends. What acts then?
tips.hint: Add a background component driven by end times.
tips.show: A close scheduler that polls auctions due by ends_at, and a closer worker that marks them closed and emits AuctionClosed.

tips.nudge: The bid service and the server holding a watcher's connection are different machines. How does the update cross?
tips.hint: Connect a pub/sub component to the servers that hold the live connections.
tips.show: Redis Pub/Sub channel auction:{id} → push servers (SSE/WebSocket) → watchers.

checks.label: Bids at the last moment handled

tips.nudge: A bid lands 5 ms after the end while the closer runs. Accepted or not, and who decides?
tips.hint: Decide whose clock defines the end and whether late bidding extends the auction.
tips.show: The database clock in the bid's conditional update is the single judge (now() < ends_at); the closer only finalises. Optional soft close: a bid in the last 2 minutes extends ends_at by 2 minutes.

tips.nudge: One celebrity item gets hundreds of bids per second. Where does that hurt?
tips.hint: Compare row contention on one auction row with serializing that auction's bids through one partition.
tips.show: Row CAS handles ~100s of bids/s per auction; beyond that route bids by auction_id to a Kafka partition with a single writer that applies them in order and pushes results.

checks.label: Bottlenecks and single points of failure named

tips.nudge: Which component sees the most load in the last minute of a hot auction?
tips.hint: Walk one hot auction's bid and fan-out paths and name what saturates.
tips.show: The hot auction row (row contention), the push tier for 10k+ watchers of one auction, the Pub/Sub node owning that channel, and the closer when many auctions end on the same second.

tips.nudge: How would you know watchers are seeing stale prices?
tips.hint: List metrics for bids, fan-out and closing.
tips.show: Bid p99 and 409 rate, outbox/relay lag, bid → push delivery lag, open connections per push server, auctions overdue to close, closer lag.
